thread:
Maya L: FYI, prod traces show ~30% regression on 8k-seq LLMs after yesterday's runtime rollout, nsys capture uploaded to nv/capture/3632101111 :eyes:

Jon P: quick skim of the nsys capture, top time culprits are:
```
1) attention_kv_cache_lookup        42.1%   18.3ms
2) fused_attention_forward         21.4%    9.3ms
3) gelu_forward                     8.9%    3.9ms
4) layernorm_forward                6.2%    2.7ms
5) softmax_over_blocks              4.5%    2.0ms
...
```

Jon P: attention_kv_cache_lookup has very low SM occupancy (~24%) and high memory latency / branch divergence. smells memory-bound and KV thrash.

Sasha R: do we see KV evict spikes in perfetto or increased small-batch frequency? I remember the prefetch change increased async evict calls.

Kevin T: perfetto shows frequent tiny evictions right after each request at high seq lengths — seems like prefetch is racing with eviction. also batching histogram shifted: more 1-2 item batches after the rollout.

Maya L: can we A/B canary: disable KV prefetch + bump KV pool size (1.5x) and prefer the fused-attn kernel for seq > 1024? quick test to isolate prefetch vs kernel-selection.

Jon P: repro command I used locally:
```
nsys profile -o /tmp/trace --capture-range=kernel -- python -m runtime.bench --model redwood/v1 --seq 8192 --batch 8
```
And the condensed top-kernel output I got (nvprof-like):
```
attention_kv_cache_lookup  42.1%  18.3ms  sm_eff 24  mem_ld_throughput=12GB/s
fused_attention_forward    21.4%   9.3ms  sm_eff 68  mem_ld_throughput=3GB/s
```

Sasha R: quick experiment idea: temporarily turn off --kv-prefetch and change kernel selector to prefer fused_attention_forward for long sequences. If latency improves, we know prefetch+evict interplay is root.

Kevin T: launching canary with flags now. perf-bot, kick off canary trace and compare.

perf-bot: Canary started (id=canary-3632101111). Trace URL: https://perf.redwood/trace/3632101111-canary
perf-bot: Canary results: p50 +10% latency improvement, top kernel time now: fused_attention_forward 45%, attention_kv_cache_lookup down to 18% (occupancy up slightly).

Maya L: nice. action items: 1) revert/guard the prefetch change behind heuristic, 2) add runtime metric for kv-evict-rate and small-batch ratio, 3) update kernel selector to bias fused-attn when evict-rate > threshold. I'll own the PR. :thumbsup:

Jon P: I'll add unit/integration test for occupancy thresholds and add a short perf test in CI.

Sasha R: I'll add perfetto dashboards for evict-rate and batch-size distribution.

Kevin T: will monitor canary and roll back if we see tail regressions.

Maya L: thanks team, I'll file the follow-up ticket with traces attached.

Jon P: +1
Sasha R: +1 :thumbsup:
thread_summary: short thread tracing a perf regression: nsys shows attention_kv_cache_lookup dominating time with low occupancy; investigation points to KV prefetch causing eviction thrash + smaller batches. Canary disabling prefetch + preferring fused-attn improved latency; action items assigned.
